Commentary.Commentary: So that's it from us! England have pulled off a superb victory courtesy some fantastic bowling in the death overs. They lead the 3-match ODI series 2-0, but there's still plenty to play for, for both teams. Remember, both teams are treating this as a good tune-up for the Champions Trophy and such pressure game will benefit both teams, despite their respective situation. The final game takes place on 29th May at Lord's at 1100 local (1000 GMT). Join us for it. Till then, cheers!

Ben Stokes (Man of the Match) says he had a lot of faith in his mate Mark Wood to pull it off in the last over. Adds some pace on the ball can make a lot of difference. Mentions you want to be in those pressure situations as players and credits Wood for showing the nerves he did in that situation, so is happy for him. On his injury, he states that it should be alright in the next couple of days so it's not serious. On prevailing today, says that it's a great opportunity for the whole team and Buttler getting some runs is a good thing for the team going forward.

Eoin Morgan says it was a real test of their character and you learn more from these games than any other. Applauds Mark Wood for showcasing his amazing talent. Feels this sort of preparation today is ideal and the fact that it was a full house in the stadium really helps. Mentions they're always trying to improve and is quite happy that he has Wood and Ball to bowl at the death, as both have a different skill set. Opines earlier in the day it was difficult to bat on, but Stokes getting the ton and Buttler getting some runs under his belt was perfect.

AB de Villiers says they had the match in the bag, especially with Miller and Morris hitting the way they did. Credits England for executing their plans well, especially in the death but is happy with how his team performed. Rues their fielding earlier in the day and reckons they could have stopped a boundary or two. Feels it's unfortunate that they fell short in the run chase. Says the trick is to minimize the damage when one or two overs don't go your way, they didn't do that and ultimately conceded 15-20 runs more than they would have liked. Is happy with their performance today and ends by saying there's still a lot to play for in the last game.

South Africa should have won the game, but couldn't come up with any answer against England bowling in the fag end, especially in the last two overs. They will rue they couldn't finish with the bat, but it was their sloppy fielding earlier in the day which really cost them the victory. It enabled Ben Stokes to score a ton and thereby post such a big total. The visitors buckled under pressure again, and it's something they'd like to work upon.

Some terrific death bowling has seen England go over the finish line and clinch the 3-match series. The Proteas got off to a solid start and then were cruising along in the middle when de Kock and de Villiers almost made a century stand. But after those two departed, with the former just missing out on a ton, it looked like England would take this game. Though a couple of quickfire knocks from Miller and Morris took the game close, they were undone by some excellent death bowling from Ball and Wood.

MARK WOOD, YOU BEAUTY! What a fantastic last over from the pacer. Excellent, excellent stuff. It's fuller in length and around off, Morris goes for the wild heave across the line but gets an inside edge onto his pads. Rolls over to the off side and a single is taken. He's done the job for his side, absolutely sensational. ENGLAND WIN BY 2 RUNS!

Dot ball! Mark Wood with a peach of a delivery, a crucial delivery to bowl at such a stage. It's short and accurate on leg, Morris looks to pull but misses. 4 needed off the final ball. What's going to happen here?

On the shorter side of the length, David Miller pulls it so hard he almost take the square leg umpire's head out. He takes evasive action and does extremely well to save a trip to the hospital. Goes to the man in the deep as a run is taken. 4 from 2 now.

Never looked out to begin with, more of a desperate attempt really.

FOUR! Go 'head, Davey. Take your side home. Short and wide outside off, it's flayed through point and across the rope for a boundary.

SIX! Now David Miller joins in on the action. Oh, boy... He's sent that outta here! Fuller in length, Miller walks across a step and smokes this straight back down the ground. Clears the fence with ease and gets a biggie to his name.

Wide outside off, Faf lets the ball go through to the keeper.
Faf du Plessis walks into the middle at No.3. Two slips in place for him.

OUT! GONE! STOKES IS THE MAN FOR TODAY! Bowls a full slower one outside off, Amla tries to drive it but does so a bit uppishly straight into the hands of Morgan who takes a nice low catch at short extra cover. First wicket for England.
Full on the pads, de Kock plays it to mid-wicket for a run.
Strays on the pads, Amla flicks it to fine leg for a run.
Full, de Kock drives it through covers for a run.

DROPPED! THE BOWLING CHANGE ALMOST WORKED! Tough chance, Stokes bowls a short of a length ball, de Kock slaps it straight back down the ground uppishly and Stokes gets a hand on it in his followthrough but cant cling onto it.
Ben Stokes to bowl now.
Bouncer and Amla lets the ball go through.
Short on the rib cage this time, de Kock goes for the pull and gets hit on the stomach and the ball rolls on the leg side. They get through for a leg bye.
Slightly short, outside off, de Kock goes to pull it but the ball just stays a little low and he misses it.
De Kock punches the length ball on the up to mid off.
Short again, Amla guides it down to thrid man for a run.
Short ball on off, de Kock tucks it on the leg side for a run.
Back of a length ball, the batsman pushes it to covers and run a single. Morgan throws at the stumps at the striker's end but misses.
The batsman gets a leading edge on that one.
FOUR! Back of a length ball, de Kock reads the length early and rocks back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Length ball, Amla drives it on the up to the left of mid off and sets off for a run. Hales has a shy and hits the stumps at the bowler's end. They go upstairs to check and Amla is safe.
FOUR! WONDERFUL TIMING! Length ball angling it into the pads, Amla stands tall and flicks it through the vacant mid-wicket area for a boundary.
Back of a length ball, Amla punches it to covers.
Lands it on a length on middle, de Kock tucks it to mid-wicket.
Tries to bounce the batsman out with a bouncer, de Kock moves away and lets the ball go through to the keeper.
De Kock flicks the length ball on middle through mid-wicket for a couple.
BOUNCER! Right on the body off the batsman, de Kock ducks under it.
LUCKY! Lands it on a length outside off, Amla tries to push it through the covers but gets an inside edge to fine leg and they run a single.
Back of a length angling into the pads of Amla, who tucks it behind square on the leg side for a couple.

FOUR! Edged and away! Short and around off, de Kock is a bit cramped for room but still goes through with the pull shot. Gets a big top edge and the ball flies over the slip cordon. Runs away to the third man fence and that'll be a boundary.
Switches the angle, comes from around the wicket and angles in a length delivery on off, Quinton stays perfectly behind the line to block.
FOUR! Short and wide, right there for him to hit and Quinton de Kock does not miss out. Cracks it past Jason Roy at point and gets a boundary to his name.
Shaping back in and catches Hashim on the thigh pad. It goes off the same and rolls away to square leg. A leg bye is taken by the batsmen.
Short of a length well outside off, Amla adjusts his body a bit and defends it down on the off side away from his body.
Straighter in line, Hashim whips it through the square leg region. The fielder in the deep mops it up and the batsmen take two.
Around off, it's kept out nicely by the southpaw.

Wood with some extra bounce off the deck, beautiful line around off and it's nipping away as Quinton de Kock has a feel for it inside the line. The ball just about whiskers past the outside edge and thuds into the keeper's gloves.
Good length delivery on middle, de Kock works it to mid-wicket. Dot ball.
Back of a length on the body, tucked behind square on the leg side for a run.
Hashim Amla got hit on the helmet and seems to have got a cut from the inside of the grill. The physio is out to have a look at him.

OUCH! That's gotta hurt! Nasty blow to Hashim Amla. Mark Wood bangs in a short ball and it's coming in, Amla looks to sway inside the line and evade, but the ball catches him on the grill of the helmet. He quickly calls out for medical attention. Seems okay though, but that must have shook him a bit.
Bit straight on middle, de Kock wrists it on the leg side and takes a quick run.
FOUR! Anything slightly off target and Hashim Amla is going to punish you. It's overpitched around off, with a beautiful straight bat Amla drives it sweetly past mid off for a boundary.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Fullish in length and on the stumps, Amla drives it back down the track for nothing.
Good length delivery outside off, cuts this away straight to the point fielder.

Shout for a leg before, but it's turned down. Quite full and very straight from Jake Ball, de Kock looks to put bat on ball as the ball goes off the pads on the off side. The batsmen comes across and the umpire doesn't signal a leg bye. Seemingly evident now why the appeal was turned down.
Hurls it in the channel outside off, Hashim Amla rises on his toes and places this behind point. Third man cuts it off as the batsmen take a single.
Marginally ahead of a length, around off, pushed to the covers to end the over.

FOUR! Beautiful shot. He's an excellent timer of the ball, Quinton de Kock. Just leans into it and drives it through the gap in the covers. Didn't hit it with much power, was all about the timing that one.
Fuller in length and outside off, Amla drives it to extra cover and sets off. There is a shy at the bowler's end from Alex Hales but it misses.
Keeps it on a length, on off, Amla positions himself behind the line and keeps it out.
Around the off stump, safely negotiated.
Seaming back in on middle and leg, takes a bit of extra bounce as Hashim Amla is caught on the thigh pad.
Outside off on a good length, it's played to point for one.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
On a length once more, around off, de Kock off the inner half plays it back down the track.
On a back of a length in the off stump channel, de Kock looks to play through the line but is beaten by the extra bounce.
FOUR! You don't want to do that against a batsman of his calibre. You just don't. Short and wide, Quinton de Kock flays it past a diving Jason Roy at point and sends it across the rope.
Good length ball moving away from the left-hander, de Kock slashes it straight to point.
Jake Ball will bowl with the second new ball from the other end.
Fuller in length and shaping back in, Hashim Amla brings his bat ahead of his pad to keep it out.
Minimal movement off the surface, just around off, kept out from within the crease.
Just ahead of a length, around off, Amla defends it rather solidly.
Good length ball around off, Amla stays behind the line and defends.
FOUR! Poor line and it's punished. Straying on the pads, Amla just helps it on its away. Sends it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Off the mark straightaway. It's full on the stumps, de Kock drives it to the mid on region and scampers across to complete the run.

We are back for the run chase. It will be Hashim Amla and Quinton de Kock to open the innings for South Africa. A lot will ride on the southpaw today, a good start is crucial. Mark Wood to start things off with the ball. Two slips in place. Let's go...
